2610.06443.title: ARO: Aligned Representation learning for multi-Omics data
2610.06443.paper_summary: The high cost of functional molecular assays, and prevalence of missing modalities and unmatched samples in computational biology, create significant barriers to comprehensive multi-omic profiling, essential for capturing and reasoning over molecules, cells, tissues, and organisms. This work proposes a model that learns meaningful representations from multi-omics cancer data supporting the reconstruction of missing and unpaired modalities. Contrary to increasingly complex, larger models, e.g. Foundation Models (FMs), ARO prioritizes practical applicability in limited or incomplete data settings. ARO optimally reconstructs missing modalities (MSE of $0.15$ on the validation and test data in the Unmasked settings), with its learned latent embeddings enabling a downstream cancer classification task. Our findings indicate that analyzing diverse molecular layers as a single integrated system offers a reliable and cost-efficient approach, reducing dependence on large-scale experimental testing, while still supporting multi-omic exploration in limited data settings.
2610.06443.paper_summary_zh: 功能性分子檢測的高成本，以及計算生物學中缺失的模態和不匹配樣本的普遍存在，對於全面的多組學分析造成了重大障礙，而這對於捕捉和推理分子、細胞、組織和生物體是至關重要的。這項工作提出了一個模型，從多組學癌症數據中學習有意義的表徵，以支持缺失和未配對模態的重建。與日益複雜、規模更大的模型（例如基礎模型）相反，ARO 在有限或不完整數據環境中優先考慮實際應用。ARO 最佳地重建缺失模態（在未遮罩設置中的驗證和測試數據上 MSE 為 $0.15$），其學習的潛在嵌入使下游的癌症分類任務成為可能。我們的研究結果表明，將多樣的分子層作為一個整合系統進行分析提供了一種可靠且具成本效益的方法，減少了對大規模實驗測試的依賴，同時仍然支持在有限數據環境中的多組學探索。
